content:
Not all portable chargers are created equal. Some designs genuinely excite me—built-in displays, the ability to charge two MacBooks simultaneously, RGB lighting effects, and a metal chassis with two windows cut out to show off the internals. Sharge's latest Shargeek 300 power bank is an absolute winner, and if you're interested, you'll definitely want to take a look during the launch promotion. Here are some of my hands-on impressions.

Sharge Shargeek 300 Power Bank Review

Sharge's brand-new Shargeek 300 power bank features a one-piece metal chassis, packs a 24,000mAh battery capacity, and can deliver up to 300W of power to your devices. The translucent design, RGB lighting effects, and built-in display are all highlights, and it's currently on sale at Amazon with a launch promotion price of $199.

Feature overview:

  • 300W total output—can charge 2 laptops and 1 smartphone simultaneously
  • CNC aluminum alloy chassis with advanced cooling system
  • 24,000mAh battery capacity—fully compliant with airline regulations
  • Equipped with dual USB-C, USB-A, and adjustable DC output (5V–28V)
  • Provides stable power for Starlink, portable refrigerators, soldering irons, camera monitors, LED fill lights, and other DC-powered devices
  • 140W USB-C input—the Shargeek 300 charges from 0% to 100% in just 44 minutes
  • Full-Tab battery cells—operating temperature reduced by up to 35%
  • 1.9-inch smart display with Sentinel BMS—real-time display of charging and discharging power curves, individual cell voltages, cycle count, usage records, and estimated remaining usage time

9to5Toys Take

Sharge is an underrated brand, if you ask me. They produce some of the most visually striking charging products on the market, and the new Shargeek 300 power bank is a perfect example of that.

This thing is absolutely gorgeous. Not everyone is into this kind of cyberpunk-style transparent aesthetic—exposing the internals, RGB lighting effects, plus a built-in display—but I'm a huge fan, and I'm sure you'll fall in love with it once you see it in person.

It features a one-piece CNC metal chassis—most power banks on the market with displays use a plastic casing... which I really hate, but I'm absolutely in love with Sharge's design here. The build quality is tank-like solid.

For me, this thing is incredibly cool-looking—beautiful enough that I'd absolutely be willing to display it in my office as decoration.

This brand's products have never let me down and have never broken, frankly, if you haven't noticed them yet, you really should. That's been the case throughout the roughly month I've been testing this new Shargeek 300W power bank.

Speaking of output power distribution, there are 300W total. When all three USB ports are used simultaneously, the two main USB-C ports can each deliver 140W at the same time, while the traditional USB-A provides an additional 20W. For me, charging three devices simultaneously is more than enough, because when I'm out and about, I rarely need to charge more than one or two devices.

Sharge says that using USB-C1 or USB-C2 alone, you can charge your MacBook Pro from 0% to 50% in about 25 to 30 minutes. I've tested it, and the numbers are spot on—my 14-inch Pro went from nearly dead to just over 50% in 27 minutes.

Alright, let's talk about the display. I absolutely love this vibe—it has a bit of a retro feel, but is super modern at the same time, I just love it.

As for functionality, it basically displays any information anyone could want to know, and even more than I want to know—real-time charging status, some discharge power curves I don't really care about but love to look at, individual cell voltages, cycle count, usage records, and so on. From what I've seen it works very smoothly, and more importantly, every time I take it out to use it, it gives me a Blade Runner or Cyberpunk 2077 kind of feeling.

For enthusiasts and professionals who really know how to use this kind of charging and voltage analytics data, this is the most comprehensive power data display I've seen on a consumer-grade power bank.

Alright, I've found my new favorite power bank. It performs as well as it looks, and it'll be staying in my everyday carry for a long time to come.
